    • Bilingual and official languages delivery (opens in a new tab)
    • Preparing accessible content and materials (opens in a new tab)
    • Sharing recordings, transcripts, and follow-up materials (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • Participants do not receive follow-up information in the official language they need.

  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Review captions and transcripts to confirm they correctly reflect language switches during the event.

    Related guidance:

    • Bilingual and official languages delivery (opens in a new tab)
    • Sharing recordings, transcripts, and follow-up materials (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • Captions or transcripts do not reflect the correct language.

    • Participants cannot rely on follow-up materials as an accurate record.
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Note issues raised about captions, interpretation, or bilingual materials, and how they were resolved.

    • Sharing recordings, transcripts, and follow-up materials (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

3.4  Large meetings, public, or high-risk events checklist

Added for 26 or more participants, town halls or organization-wide sessions, public/formal sessions, explicit high-risk content, or recording the session. Sharing notes alone does not trigger this checklist.

Before
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Test the full setup together, not each piece separately, confirm remote participants can hear in-room speakers and vice versa if hybrid.
    • Test captions, interpretation, audio, screen sharing, and participation tools together, using the actual event setup.
    • For public, recorded, high-profile, or high-risk events, consider involving accessibility specialists or test users.

    Related guidance:

    • Choosing an accessible platform, venue, or tools (opens in a new tab)
    • Planning and testing accessibility services (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • Captions, interpretation, audio, video, screen sharing, or participation tools fail during the event.
    • Technical issues are discovered only once participants have joined.
    • Accessibility features that work in a small test don't hold up with a full, large, or hybrid audience.
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • For legal, policy, or media-sensitive content, have a second person check materials before they are finalized or shared.
    • Confirm names, figures, and technical terms are correct, since errors carry more weight in high-risk content.

    Related guidance:

    • Preparing accessible content and materials (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • Inaccurate information being shared on a sensitive or high-profile topic.
    • Misunderstandings that are harder to correct once shared publicly or with senior leaders.

3.5  Visual content checklist

Added when visual content is selected. Pre-recorded media has its own checklist with instructions for audio-only and video content.

During
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Verbalize key information shown in slides, charts, diagrams, demonstrations, videos, whiteboards, and screen sharing. Focus on information needed to understand the discussion or make decisions.

    Related guidance:

    • Preparing accessible content and materials (opens in a new tab)
    • Preparing speakers and presenters (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • Information available only visually.

Note: the delivery format and event type checklists above may also include context-specific reminders to describe visuals (for example, printed materials in a room, or content shared on screen). This item is a general reminder shown whenever visual content applies, and is not meant to replace those more specific items.

3.6  Recording and follow-up materials checklist

Added for recording or shared follow-up materials. Recording-specific actions apply only when recording is selected; official-record actions also require the Public/formal session feature.

Before
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Make this decision before the invitation goes out so you can tell participants in advance.

    • Recordings are shared later without captions, transcripts, or accessible alternatives when needed.
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Participants feel pressure to take detailed notes because follow-up materials are unclear.
During
  • Show guidance and barriers

After
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    How to do this:

3.7  Indigenous, cultural, and community considerations checklist

Added automatically when your planning path includes Indigenous, cultural, or community considerations.

Before
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Ask early whether specific supports, protocols, language needs, or preparation time are needed, and provide materials early so participants have time to review, consult, or prepare.
    • Do not assume all First Nations, Inuit, and Métis participants or communities have the same needs, preferences, or protocols.

    Related guidance:

    • Indigenous, cultural, and community considerations (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • Participants or communities are not given enough time or the right supports to prepare or take part.
    • Assumptions about protocols or needs create barriers instead of removing them.
    • Language, geography, technology, or time zones limit who can access or take part in the event.

3.8  Accessibility supports checklist

Added when accessibility supports are selected. Apply only the instructions for services you will use; online platform and lobby checks apply to virtual or hybrid delivery.

Before
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Check whether captions or interpretation still work reliably at your expected participant count, not just in a small test.
    • Confirm this for each platform or tool used, since accessibility features can behave differently across them.

    Related guidance:

    • Planning and testing accessibility services (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • Captions, interpretation, or other accessibility features are not supported at scale.
    • Accessibility features that work in a small test do not hold up with a large group.
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Review default permission settings — they can unintentionally block camera use needed for sign language.
    • Check that waiting room or lobby settings don't delay entry for participants who need extra time to join.

    Related guidance:

    • Choosing an accessible platform, venue, or tools (opens in a new tab)
    • Assigning roles and support (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • Default permission settings unintentionally block camera use needed for sign language.
    • Waiting room or lobby settings delay entry for participants who need extra time to join.
    • Participants cannot unmute or turn on video when they need to communicate visually.
    • Permission settings are chosen for moderation convenience without checking the accessibility impact.
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Agree in advance on a quiet way to flag issues to the host (chat message, hand signal) without interrupting the session.
    • Rehearsing this once avoids confusion and delay when a real issue comes up live.

    Related guidance:

    • Planning and testing accessibility services (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • No one knows who is responsible for fixing an accessibility issue once the session starts.
    • Support staff interrupt the session to report a problem instead of using a quiet channel.
    • Delays happen because the response process was never rehearsed with the full team.
    • Issues that a single presenter cannot fix alone go unresolved for the rest of the session.
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Decide in advance who will troubleshoot and how you'll notify participants if something fails.
    • For technical failures, audio (in-room, online, or both), captions, interpretation, participation tools, platform, or livestream, have a fallback ready (phone line, alternate device, or secondary streaming link) so the event doesn't stall while you fix the issue.
    • For booked accessibility services (captioning, interpretation), line up a standby provider you can call on short notice.
    • Decide in advance who is authorized to make the call to pause, switch, or reschedule.

    Related guidance:

    • Preparing a backup plan (opens in a new tab)
    • Assigning roles and support (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • The meeting continues even though some participants cannot hear, see, follow, or participate because no one activates a planned response.
    • Participants do not know what to do when access issues occur, or when a session suddenly goes offline.
    • Organizers cannot quickly switch to another way of sharing information or supporting participation.
    • A vendor cancellation, technical failure, or livestream outage leaves the event without a needed service and no standby ready.
    • Participants do not know what to do when access issues occur.
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    Related guidance:

    • Planning and testing accessibility services (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • Participants cannot follow spoken information because of hearing, audio quality, language, or processing barriers.

    • Automated captions may be inaccurate for technical terms, names, acronyms, or bilingual content.
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Confirm requested accommodations with participants privately and book any needed services early.

    Related guidance:

    • Accessible meetings and events guidance (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • A contact is named but the requested accommodation is never arranged.
During
  • Show guidance and barriers

  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • After
    • Show guidance and barriers

      How to do this:

      • Send the same follow-up package to both audiences — don't let one group get more complete information than the other.
      • Make sure recordings or summaries capture information from both the room and the online platform.

      Related guidance:

      • Preparing accessible content and materials (opens in a new tab)
      • Sharing recordings, transcripts, and follow-up materials (opens in a new tab)

      Helps prevent barriers such as:

3.10  Accessible interaction checklist

Added when Interaction is selected.

Before
  • Show guidance and barriers

During
  • Show guidance and barriers

After
  • Show guidance and barriers

    • Accessible meetings and events guidance (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • Only participants who could use the main activity tool receive its outcomes.

3.11  Pre-recorded media checklist

Added when Pre-recorded content is selected; use the actions appropriate to audio-only, silent video, or video with audio.

Before
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • For audio-only material, provide an accurate transcript.
    • For video with audio, check captions for speech and meaningful sounds; provide a transcript or other accessible alternative as needed.
    • For silent video or visual information not explained in the soundtrack, provide a spoken or text description of the essential information.
    • Check captions and transcripts for errors before the session.

    Related guidance:

    • Accessible meetings and events guidance (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • A recording contains information participants cannot hear or see.
  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Test the actual room equipment or online sharing method, including sound and caption visibility.
    • For hybrid delivery, test what both audiences receive.
    • Have a backup such as an accessible transcript, description, or alternate playback method.

    Related guidance:

    • Preparing a backup plan (opens in a new tab)
    • Accessible meetings and events guidance (opens in a new tab)

    Helps prevent barriers such as:

    • Captions or audio work for the host but are unavailable to participants.

  • Show guidance and barriers

    How to do this:

    • Explain what will be played and where captions, a transcript, or a visual description are available.
    • Pause if essential audio, visuals, captions, or alternatives are unavailable, then use the backup.

    Related guidance:

    Helps prevent barriers such as:
